title: the WSG hunting proficiency and fishing slice - the hunting proficiency, fishing and Table 32, printed p. 57 with the spot-guideline tail on p. 58
audit_comment: The Table 32 dice grid cell by cell (the die and the modifier per spot quality per time of day), the hunting proficiency kill rules (the one-hit size M kill, the two-hit size L kill, the distance kill of a wounded size M, the single-hit wounded size L, the Proficiency Check before the 1d6 roll) and the fishing mechanics (the net bonus, the zero gate, the proficiency bonus, the group and hour penalties, the fished-out rule) - every cell, const, bool and switch verified against the model.

banner.title: R465: the WSG HUNTING PROFICIENCY AND FISHING slice - the hunting proficiency (the one-hit size M kill, the two-hit size L kill, the 50% distance kill of a wounded size M with a single attempt, the single-hit wounded size L with multiple attempts, the successful Proficiency Check before the 1d6 roll, the missile-weapon requirement, no boost to the encounter chance or the prey size, the repeatable expeditions), fishing (the one-hour baited hook-and-line base, the net +50%, the zero-or-lower no-fish gate, the proficiency +2 in fair or good spots only, the cumulative -1 per extra group member, the cumulative -2 per hour beyond the first in the same spot, the fished-out rule, the spot-quality guidelines) and Table 32 (the spot-by-time dice grid), printed p. 57 with the spot-guideline tail on p. 58.
banner.provenance: Ground truth three-way: the archive djvu word layer vs the pixel reads of the native decode of the printed p. 57 image (a pure-Python JPEG decoder, 1179x1516) vs vision reads of contrast-stretched cell crops. The text layer drops the Fair-Day cell and garbles four Good cells; the pixels settled them: Fair-Day 1d6-2 (glyph holes=1, the canonical 6 template at 0.947), Good-Day 1d8-2 (the digit shows the stacked-loop waist of an 8, template 0.775 vs 0.738 for the 6), Good-Night 1d6+2 (proven by the book own A/B/C example: 1d6+4 for the proficient A = 1d6+2 + 2), Good-Dawn 1d8+2 (the same 8 waist; the plus vertical stroke survives as faint 158-238 grayscale traces through the bar while the true minus on the same page shows pure background around its bar). The Fair and Good row labels are pixel-and-vision confirmed. The p. 58 tail completes the p. 57 sentence: fish congregate where they can be shaded by trees or overhanging terrain; such a spot is fair or good while an unshaded spot nearby on the same body of water is a poor one.
banner.sentinel: All 18 Table 32 cells pinned (the die and the modifier per row per time band); the hunting proficiency and fishing mechanics are audit examples, including the book own A/B/C three-fisherman hour-by-hour example.

consts.name: wfsRowCount
consts.comment: the Table 32 row count: the poor, fair and good spot-quality rows

consts.name: wfsNetBonusPct
consts.comment: a net increases the take to 50% more than the modified die roll

consts.name: wfsProfBonus
consts.comment: a character with fishing proficiency gets a +2 modifier in any fair or good area

consts.name: wfsGroupPenalty
consts.comment: each extra member of the fishing group takes a cumulative -1: -1 for the second character, -2 for the third, and so on

consts.name: wfsSpotHourPenalty
consts.comment: each hour beyond the first spent in the same spot takes a further cumulative -2 per hour

consts.name: wfsFishedOutDays
consts.comment: a fished-out spot will not yield any more fish for at least one day

consts.name: wfsProfWoundedMDistancePct
consts.comment: a proficient hunter has a 50% chance of killing a wounded size M creature from a distance instead of closing with it

consts.name: wfsProfWoundedLHits
consts.comment: a proficient hunter kills a wounded size L creature with a single hit instead of the two or three a group might need

bools.name: wfsProfCheckBeforeRoll
bools.comment: the hunting proficiency feats require a successful Proficiency Check when game is encountered, before the 1d6 size-and-number roll

bools.name: wfsProfNeedsMissile
bools.comment: the proficiency feats require a missile weapon of the appropriate sort

bools.name: wfsProfNoEncounterBoost
bools.comment: a proficient hunter does not increase the chance of encountering game, nor affect the size of the prey encountered

bools.name: wfsProfRepeatable
bools.comment: hunting expeditions may be undertaken as often as desired - animals are not rooted, and the same area can be searched again

bools.name: wfsProfWoundedMOneAttempt
bools.comment: only one distance-kill attempt on a wounded size M creature; if it fails, the creature has escaped

bools.name: wfsProfWoundedLMultipleAttempts
bools.comment: multiple attempts are permitted on a wounded size L creature if it is not dispatched on the first attempt

bools.name: wfsZeroNoFish
bools.comment: a die-roll result of zero or lower catches no fish regardless of the gear used

bools.name: wfsProfBonusFairGoodOnly
bools.comment: the fishing proficiency bonus applies only in fair or good areas - prowess does not help in a poor spot

bools.name: wfsFishedOutAllZero
bools.comment: a spot is fished out as soon as every fisherman gets a result of zero or lower in the same hour

bools.name: wfsBoatBetterThanShore
bools.comment: fishing from a boat moored in the middle of a body of water is better than fishing from shore

bools.name: wfsShadedSpotFairGood
bools.comment: in hot or sunny weather fish congregate where they can be shaded by trees or overhanging terrain, or in rain; such a spot is fair or good

bools.name: wfsUnshadedSpotPoor
bools.comment: an unshaded spot nearby on the same body of water will be a poor one

bools.name: wfsSwampBogPoor
bools.comment: a swamp or bog is generally a poor place for fishing

bools.name: wfsStagnantCreekPoor
bools.comment: a stagnant, shallow creek is a poor place for fishing

switches.name: wfsProfHitsToKill
switches.comment: hits to kill with hunting proficiency by size band: one for size S, one for size M (instead of two), two for size L (instead of four)

tables.name: wfsFishSuccess
tables.audit_comment: the Table 32 fishing success grid (the die and the modifier per spot quality per time of day)

examples.note: the poor spot: 1d4-2 by day, 1d4 at night, 1d4+2 at dawn or dusk
examples.expr: m['wfsDayDie'](0) != 4 or m['wfsDayMod'](0) != -2 or m['wfsNightDie'](0) != 4 or m['wfsNightMod'](0) != 0 or m['wfsDawnDie'](0) != 4 or m['wfsDawnMod'](0) != 2

examples.note: the fair spot: 1d6-2 by day, 1d6-1 at night, 1d6+2 at dawn or dusk (the OCR-dropped day cell, pixel-confirmed)
examples.expr: m['wfsDayDie'](1) != 6 or m['wfsDayMod'](1) != -2 or m['wfsNightDie'](1) != 6 or m['wfsNightMod'](1) != -1 or m['wfsDawnDie'](1) != 6 or m['wfsDawnMod'](1) != 2

examples.note: the good spot: 1d8-2 by day, 1d6+2 at night (the book example cell), 1d8+2 at dawn or dusk
examples.expr: m['wfsDayDie'](2) != 8 or m['wfsDayMod'](2) != -2 or m['wfsNightDie'](2) != 6 or m['wfsNightMod'](2) != 2 or m['wfsDawnDie'](2) != 8 or m['wfsDawnMod'](2) != 2

examples.note: the book hour-1 example A: the proficient lone fisherman at a good spot at night rolls 1d6+4
the book hour-1 example B: the first extra group member rolls 1d6+1
the book hour-1 example C: the second extra group member rolls 1d6
the book hour-2 example A: 1d6+2 (the night modifier less the hour penalty plus the proficiency bonus)
the book hour-3 example B: 1d6-3 (the cumulative hour penalty twice plus the group penalty)
the book hour-3 example C: 1d6-4, and in hour 4 all three can reach zero or lower - the fished-out hour
the net: a take of 4 fish rises to 6 (50% more, cross-multiplied)
the fished-out spot yields nothing for at least one day
the hunting proficiency kill ladder: one hit for size S and M, two for size L
the distance kill of a wounded size M creature: a 50% chance, one attempt only
the wounded size L creature drops to a single hit for a proficient hunter

table_checks.note: the dawn-or-dusk modifier is the daytime modifier plus 4 in every row
table_checks.expr: m['wfsDawnMod'](0) - m['wfsDayMod'](0) != 4 or m['wfsDawnMod'](1) - m['wfsDayMod'](1) != 4 or m['wfsDawnMod'](2) - m['wfsDayMod'](2) != 4

table_checks.note: the daytime die ladder climbs 4, 6, 8 across the poor, fair and good rows, and so does the dawn-or-dusk die
table_checks.expr: m['wfsDayDie'](0) != 4 or m['wfsDayDie'](1) != 6 or m['wfsDayDie'](2) != 8 or m['wfsDawnDie'](0) != 4 or m['wfsDawnDie'](1) != 6 or m['wfsDawnDie'](2) != 8
